findings.summary: Spec requirement 5's mandated complementary assertion -- that a genuine new attempt WITHOUT its required prior REJECT remains rejected -- is absent. The only complementary test added, test_a_rework_still_returns_a_derived_identity, drives ContractActor({'continuous_review': ['REJECT','APPROVE']}), i.e. a rework that DOES have its required prior REJECT, and asserts only that the rework implement gets a derived (unpinned) identity. No test asserts the without-REJECT case is refused, so a change that weakens the ordering rule globally (forbidden by requirement 4) would pass the suite.

The reported failure is not fixed. prior_generation_state_roots(run_root, 2) yields exactly one prior state root, so at generation 2 _build_plan collects a single candidate plan and max() over one element returns it unchanged -- identical to the previous selection -- yet the spec's Problem section reports generation 2 failing with ORDER_VIOLATION. Separately, every path that ends the prefix at implement (broken review link at dd_replay.py:309, missing frozen intent at dd_replay.py:332, a path deliberately preserved by test_a_review_whose_intent_is_missing_reruns_for_real) still dispatches and materializes a fresh continuous review on the replayed implement -- exactly the materialization the carrier refuses. Requirement 3 is unmet.

Preferring the review-bearing prefix can disable replay entirely. If generation 1 sealed a reviewed chain and generation 2 sealed a real implement above it touching product code before crashing, generation 3 now discards g2's viable [configure, implement] plan for g1's four-step plan; _prepare then sees product.py outside RESERVED_PREFIXES, returns False (dd_replay.py:534-538), and replay() sets _disabled with no fallback to the runner-up plan -- so nothing replays and a fresh implement actor is re-dispatched against a tree that already carries the work, the F4 BLOCKED jam. The new test builds exactly this shape but asserts only on _build_plan and never invokes _prepare.

The test named as the reported-sequence reproduction exercises neither the changed behaviour nor the carrier. test_a_fully_reviewed_chain_replays_through_to_acceptance builds a single prior generation, so max() has one candidate and the result is independent of the _build_plan change; it also asserts continuous_review is replayed, so no continuous-review handoff is materialized at all, and with ContractActor/make_deps fakes neither the materializer nor the feedback index ordering is touched. Requirement 5's 'continuous-review handoff materialization succeeds' and 'no illegal new attempt is created' are asserted only by proxy.

Product-tree identity between e2035e37 and aba711c2 could not be mechanically verified: the mandated git diff --exit-code was declined by the permission layer, so equality rests on file inspection alone. Additionally the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit befb93387414d5dbfadcfdced1080d38f3008899 while the review context supplies e2035e37ab6d1647c32ec340d68e3436d71d4bc4 as the product commit; this is consistent with a compliant metadata-only implement materialization stacked on befb9338, but was not confirmed against the object graph. Recorded for the seal, which verifies HEAD independently; not counted toward the REJECT.
